newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN B SHARES END UP, BUT TRADE REMAINS DULL.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN B SHARES END UP, BUT TRADE REMAINS DULL.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed up in sluggish trade on Friday, thanks to sporadic selective buying by institutions, brokers said.
The index gained 1.49 points or 1.15 percent to 131.48 on turnover of HK$44 million against HK$45 million on Thursday.
The domestic A share index lost 3.56 points or 0.87 percent to 403.83, with turnover expanding to 6.2 billion yuan from Thursday's 4.4 billion.
"Buying interest remained weak," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said, given the thin turnover.

Brokers said recently listed B shares, such as Beijing Orient, are likely to outperform the market on investor expectation that they would post robust results in the 1997 interim corporate reporting season that ended on August 30.
Beijing Orient rose HK$0.05 to HK$4.00 with 1.88 million shares traded. It was the day's second most actively traded B share issue.

The company, a maker of lamps and colour television components, said earlier this week it posted net profits of 68.72 million yuan for January-June period under international accounting standards, up 29 percent from the year-ago period.
"Backed by its solid earnings, the stock may become the market's star later this year," the analyst said.
Investors may continue to hold back from large-scale trading this month, waiting for all B share companies to release their interim results, an analyst at Everbright Securities said.
Only three of the 49 Shenzhen B share listed firms have announced their 1997 interim results.
Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Real Estate & Properties was the best performer, surging HK$0.17 or 7.02 percent to HK$2.59 on volume of 42,000 shares.
Brokers said the gain was insignificant because of the flimsy trading volume.
Analysts have said they expected the company to report weak interim earnings due to the continued sluggishness in Shenzhen's office property market in the first half of this year.
Chongqing Chang'an Automobile, one of China's top mini sedan producers, climbed HK$0.14 or 4.67 percent to HK$ 3.14 on volume of 98,907 shares.
Guangdong Power Developement inched up HK$0.23 to HK$5.88 on 775,000 shares.
Bengang Steel closed unchanged at HK$2.10 on the session's heaviest trading volume of 4.4 million shares.
Brokers said institutions have been supporting Bengang, which is still traded below its recent offer price of HK$2.38 per share.
Bengang listed 400 million B shares in Shenzhen in early July and became the first B share to close below its offer price on its first day of trading.
Analysts have attributed its miserable debut to weak market sentiment, its large share capitalisation and pessimism over China's flagging steel industry.

In the A share market, Jiujiang Chemical Fibre suffered the heaviest loss, sliding 0.91 yuan to close 10 percent limit-down at 8.17 yuan after the company posted disappointing interim profits on Friday.

Chemical company Sichuan Meifeng was among the biggest A share losers on a continued sell-off sparked by the firm's releasing of its worse-than-expected interim results earlier this week, brokers said.
The issue tumbled 1.44 yuan to 21.87 yuan on Friday after diving 20 percent in the past two days.
